scope: Bounded T30 code review only; no edits/tests/network; not a human historical grade or workflow adoption verdict
actual_findings: Initial saved response lacked a digest checked on recovery.
Cached input could exceed total input, allowing negative estimated cost.
Terminal result usage was not rechecked against its raw response checkpoint on reopening.
root_resolution: Request, response and terminal-result digests now verified on open/read; native input/config mismatch fails before schema changes.
Invalid cached usage becomes unknown usage/cost and prevents further sends.
Terminal result fingerprints and provider-field correspondence verified on open/results; fresh-process regression check covers lowered usage.
final_report_received: I found one remaining integrity gap: terminal result_json is not rechecked against its hashed response checkpoint when the journal is reopened. If its saved usage is changed, paid budget checks could use the altered amount. I sent this to the primary agent. No files were changed, and I ran no tests or provider calls.
post_review_status: Primary implemented the final fix and added its regression test; final full gate covers it. No claim of a further independent verdict.
